question.text: How will the Agit Kabayel vs. Nelson Hysa fight end on November 28, 2026?
question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves as the way the boxing match ends between Agit Kabayel and Nelson Hysa, currently scheduled for Saturday, November 28, 2026. Please note that "other outcome" includes any other outcome, including a Hysa victory, a draw, or the boxing match for any reason not being held before November 29, 2026 (local time).

research:

### 1. Resolution source
- No official results page exists yet. The result will come from the official outcome reported by the WBC, DAZN and Queensberry.

Filip Hrgovic holds the IBF belt. [WBC](https://wbcboxing.com/en/agit-kabayel-to-defend-wbc-world-heavyweight-title-against-nelson-hysa/), [Punch](https://punchng.com/hrgovic-sets-conditions-for-second-itauma-clash/)

## 1. Resolution source
- The question has no official results URL, so the outcome will come from the official fight result as reported by DAZN, BoxRec and the press. The DAZN background article returned HTTP 403 and I could not read it. Its headline says "first IBF defence", but every other source calls this a WBC title fight. [DAZN](https://www.dazn.com/en-US/news/boxing/agit-kabayel-sets-first-ibf-defence-nelson-hysa-dusseldorf/m3q2qk73qx1b1s8ns5zb9g4iy)
- 2026-10-29: The fight has not happened yet, so there is no result.

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has settled the question yet. The fight is on and promotion is active, with no reports of injury or postponement. A German-language search for injury, cancellation or press-conference news found nothing relevant.
- 2026-06-27: The WBC promoted Kabayel from interim to full champion after Oleksandr Usyk vacated. Kabayel is 27-0 with 19 KOs. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agit_Kabayel)
- Hysa is 42 years old (born 1984-09-06) and 25-0 with 23 KOs. He turned pro at 37 in 2022, is unranked by the WBC and has fought club-level opposition under Queensberry. - By the question's buckets, those six stoppages split: rounds 1-3: 3 of 6, rounds 4-6: 2 of 6, rounds 7-12: 1 of 6.
- His last decision win was 2021-06-05 (Kevin Johnson, UD). Over his career he has 8 decisions in 27 wins, and 5 of those were in fights scheduled for 10 or 12 rounds. Several of his slower or later stoppages came against stronger opponents (Sánchez, Zhang). Hysa is weaker on paper but untested.
- Hysa has no losses and has never been stopped. His opposition includes Patrick Korte (TKO round 2, June 2025), Abel Pesut, Ariel Bracamonte, Danny Williams and Pavel Sour. Kabayel stopped Sour in round 1 in 2022. I could not find how Hysa did against Sour.
- Huge favourites in heavyweight title fights against older, untested challengers usually win by stoppage. I found no specific statistics for this.

forecasts.reasoning:
**(a) Time left:** About 30 days. The fight is on Saturday, November 28, 2026, and resolves around 2026-11-29 00:00 UTC.

**(b) Status quo outcome:** The fight goes ahead and Kabayel wins, most likely by stoppage. As of 2026-10-28 it is confirmed, more than 40,000 tickets are reportedly sold, and there are no injury reports.

**(c) Base rates:**
- **Kabayel's recent form:** his last six fights were all stoppages. Three came in rounds 1-3 (Sour R1, Smakici R3, Knyba R3), two in rounds 4-6 (Makhmudov R4, Zhang R6) and one in rounds 7-12 (Sánchez R7). His last decision was in 2021.
- **Heavy favourites:** at -1800 to -2000 the underdog wins roughly 5-8% of the time once the vig is removed.
- **Cancellations:** title fights a month out get cancelled or postponed (injury, illness, visa problems) perhaps 4-7% of the time.

**(d) Strongest evidence:**
- **Odds:** FanDuel -1800 and BetUS -2000 (October 2026) imply about a 92-94% Kabayel win, conditional on the fight happening.
- **Hysa's record:** 25-0 with 23 KOs, but against weak opposition (Boente). He is 42, and he stopped Narmo in round 2 in August 2026.
- **Kabayel's style:** a pressure body-puncher who often breaks opponents down in the middle rounds. He beat lower-tier opponents early, as with Knyba in R3 on 2026-01-10.
- **Expert picks:** Boente says Kabayel inside five rounds. Split-Decision and Champinon both pick a Kabayel stoppage.
- **No method or round market exists**, so there is no strong anchor for the round split.

**(e) Unexpected scenario:** Hysa is a genuine one-punch puncher. He could land early while Kabayel starts slowly, and a 42-year-old untested fighter has nothing to lose. Alternatively, an injury or illness during fight week could cancel the bout. Either resolves as "Other." A third path: the 42-year-old Hysa survives by holding and moving, and the fight goes to the cards.

**How I got the split:**
- **Other outcome (12%):** about 6% Hysa wins, about 5% cancellation and about 1% draw or no contest. That leaves Kabayel at about 88%.
- **Rounds 1-3 vs 4-6:** I started from his six-fight stoppage spread (50/33/17). I moved some weight from rounds 1-3 towards 4-6 because Kabayel tends to start slowly and work the body. I also left a decision share, because Hysa is durable enough to be unbeaten even if untested.
- **Rounds 7-12 and decision:** stoppages this late are less likely against a fading 42-year-old, but they remain plausible.
